title: Julie Margenthaler named inaugural endowed chair for surgical excellence in breast cancer
text:
Julie Margenthaler, MD, FACS, has been installed as the inaugural Endowed Chair for Surgical Excellence in Breast Cancer through The Foundation for Barnes-Jewish Hospital, according to an April 29 announcement. The honor recognizes Margenthaler’s national reputation for surgical expertise and her commitment to patient care at Siteman Cancer Center.
The new endowed chair was made possible by donors, many of whom are former patients of Margenthaler. This recognition is intended to support innovative care and research in breast cancer surgery. “It’s about how many patients she took care of and how many patients she helped and how many patients she cured,” Timothy J. Eberlein, MD, director of Siteman Cancer Center, said during the installation ceremony. “I don’t think there is a better person who could be better feted with this endowed chair than Julie Margenthaler because, as many of you in the audience will attest, she is the most caring, compassionate but superb physician.”
Margenthaler’s approach combines clinical care with research and education. She serves as both a surgical oncologist and director of Breast Surgical Services at the Joanne Knight Breast Health Center at Siteman Cancer Center. Her research focuses on minimally invasive approaches to breast cancer staging using imaging combined with molecular techniques and identifying non-BRCA genes responsible for breast cancer development in young women under age 40.
In addition to her clinical work, Margenthaler is a professor of surgery and director of the Surgical Fellowship for Advanced Training in Breast Disease at Washington University School of Medicine (WashU Medicine). “This endowed chair will allow us to continue to push the envelope in research for advances to come 10 or 20 years from now,” Margenthaler said. “And it will allow us a regenerating mechanism for research, specifically research that may not be traditionally funded by the National Institutes of Health. It also creates a legacy that will allow us to recruit the best people who want to continue our mission.”
Pam Nicholson is one patient whose generosity contributed to establishing this chair position: “You’re in such a vulnerable position when you’re first diagnosed,” Nicholson said. “Dr. Margenthaler is just that right person who is so calming, and she instills confidence… I think Dr. Margenthaler is a jewel for the hospital, for St. Louis and for all the Midwest.” Nationally recognized roles held by Margenthaler include serving as president of the American Society of Breast Surgeons; currently section editor for Annals of Surgical Oncology; editorial board member on Journal of Surgical Research; reviewer across twelve journals; authoring over 240 peer-reviewed publications.
Siteman Cancer Center at Barnes-Jewish Hospital was founded in 1999 and is located in Saint Louis, Missouri [according to available information]. Its current president is Timothy Eberlein.
Looking ahead, supporters say this endowment provides resources needed both now and into future decades as researchers pursue breakthroughs not always supported by traditional funding sources.
